lines.en: Leaving Aileen, Mark, and Jang Hayoung to sort things out outside, I dragged the unconscious Han Myungoh back to the treatment room.
Honestly, this was unexpected.
To think that ‘Han Myungoh’ was still alive.
Department Manager Han Myungoh.
The man who had tried to steal the last hit on the Dark Keeper from me and received Demon King Asmodeus’s curse before we had even reached Main Scenario 3.
He had disappeared before we entered Chungmuro, so I had assumed he was dead. I never imagined I would meet this man in the ‘Demon Realm,’ of all places.
I bound Han Myungoh to a chair in the treatment room, using Story-suppressing restraints I had borrowed from Aileen.
「Kim Dokja thought. The department manager has aged quite a bit, too.」

Fine wrinkles had multiplied across Han Myungoh’s face. His skin had also turned black all over. The wrinkles were one thing, but the skin was probably a sign of species mutation (種變異). The longer I looked, the more I seemed to glimpse his old face. But so many traces of his human days had disappeared that he was difficult to recognize without a close look.
Yoo Sangah. Lee Gilyoung. And my mother and the school bully Song Minwoo······.
All people whose information I had been unable to check with [Character List] so far.

All people who had known me immediately before the scenarios began, or even earlier. Han Myungoh was the same. Someone who had come to live in this world because of me, whose information the original [Character List] could not read.
“I know you’re awake. Open your eyes.”
“Ugh······ you little······.”
I questioned Han Myungoh······ the Spy, that is. No, the self-proclaimed ‘Aurelius.’
“Aurelius. Did you come up with that yourself?”
Seeing Han Myungoh’s eyes widen, I felt the last traces of uncertainty give way to complete conviction. Aurelius. That had been the decisive clue that convinced me this man was ‘Han Myungoh.’
「Web nooovels? Listen, Kim Dokja-ssi. Who has time to read that rubbish?」
Those were the words I had heard when I was caught reading webnovels back when I still worked at ‘Mino Soft.’
「If you’re going to read books, read something like this. If you have no intention of improving your qualifications, at least read a decent book.」

As he said that, Han Myungoh had been holding 『Meditations』, written by the wise Roman emperor Marcus Aurelius. A book with only its first few pages darkened, as though he had only skimmed the beginning······.
“You used to carry 『Meditations』 around without ever reading it. I see you still haven’t lost that pretentious streak.”
“W-who the hell are you!”
The struggling Han Myungoh did not recognize me at all.
Good thing I had changed my face beforehand.
Otherwise, I might have been the one walking into a trap.
I asked with a sly smile.
“Who do you think I am?”
At that moment, something flashed through Han Myungoh’s eyes.
“D-don’t tell me······!”
Han Myungoh was still Han Myungoh, after all.

Even a department manager appointed through connections needed a certain knack for reading people to survive at a company. Just as Han Myungoh’s slowly widening mouth was finally about to open, I quietly placed a finger against it.
“Shh.”
“Mmph. Mmmph. Mmmmph!”
“If you say that, you’ll die right here. So keep it to yourself. Understand?”
I had made that decision out of concern that some other transcendent being might be listening.
There were no dokkaebi channels here. But the absence of a channel did not mean there were no other ways to spy on someone.
[‘Fourth Wall’ says, ‘The Demon King, ‘Devil of Lust and Wrath,’ is watching the foolish Kim Dokja.’]
······Not bad. You could tell me things like this, too?
「A hem.」
Devil of Lust and Wrath······.
Like constellations, Demon Kings also had their own modifiers. They were ‘fallen constellations,’ after all. Of course, some refused to use them out of resentment toward the constellations······.

If I remembered correctly, ‘Devil of Lust and Wrath’ was Demon King Asmodeus’s epithet. It appeared that Han Myungoh had become his subordinate. A high-ranking subordinate, at that, whose vision Asmodeus could share.
“If you’re going to keep peeping, why don’t you at least pay some coins?”
Watching me speak into thin air, Han Myungoh’s eyes widened again, almost to the point of tearing. He had realized who I was addressing.
Tzzzzzt. Small sparks flickered in the air.
If we continued talking like this, there was a good chance Asmodeus would learn information about me.
I would certainly reveal this ‘story’ someday, but the time had not yet come.
After a moment’s thought, I took a sword out of my coat’s subspace.
It was the [Four Tiger Evil Cutting Sword].
A sword I had not drawn in a very long time, since destroying the [Absolute Throne]. By borrowing the power of the Constellations of the Big Dipper, it could temporarily evolve into a Star Relic.
A sword that could sever a constellation’s bond (緣) imbued in a Star Relic.

Originally, I had needed the help of the Constellations of the Big Dipper to manifest that power. Now that I had become a constellation, however, I could draw on a little of the sword’s power without their help.
[‘Four Tiger Evil Cutting Sword’ responds to your Story!]
“If you won’t pay, fuck off.”
As I said that, I swung the sword over Han Myungoh’s head.
The light swing sent fierce sparks bursting through the air, followed by a message.
[The connection between Demon King ‘Asmodeus’ and his subordinate is temporarily severed.]
Han Myungoh was no longer merely shocked; his face had turned deathly pale.
He probably never imagined I would have enough power to sever the bond between him and a Demon King. I spoke to him in warning.
“My name here is ‘Yoo Joonghyuk.’ Nod if you understand.”

Han Myungoh stared at me with conflicted eyes, thought about something for a long while, and finally managed a nod. He valued his own life, so he had probably made the right decision. When I freed his mouth, Han Myungoh looked up at me, panting for breath.
“How, how on earth······ I was told you were dead······.”
“I didn’t die. That’s why I’m here, alive.”
Han Myungoh asked, terrified.
“W-what are you going to do with me?”
“Well. I’m thinking about it.”
“S-spare me! We spent a long time together, didn’t we!”
“And I don’t have a single good memory from all that time.”
“I-I’m the [Spy]. I can help with the revolution! I can see other people’s positions!”

The fact that he would say even that in this situation suggested Han Myungoh really was the [Spy]. The [Spy] had never actually appeared in the 111th round of ‘Ways of Survival,’ so it would not be strange for someone unexpected to turn up in that position.
“We don’t need a Spy. I found the Executioners just fine without one.”
At those words, poor Han Myungoh’s eyes wavered again.
Then, as if something had occurred to him, Han Myungoh abruptly asked,
“Come to think of it······ how on earth did you recognize the Executioners?”
I had a fair idea of what he was up to, but decided to play along for a moment.
“I didn’t know they were Executioners.”
“What? Then how could you······.”

I was telling the truth. ‘Ways of Survival’ did describe the appearances of some Executioners, but I did not remember all of them. Besides, those descriptions had been mentioned only in passing, making recognition from them alone impossible.
I had not killed them knowing they were [Executioners].
I had merely used [Omniscient Reader’s Viewpoint] from time to time and learned that they held ‘special positions.’
「And for Kim Dokja, that information was enough.」
Knowing none of this, Han Myungoh shouted,
“T-the people you killed could have been innocent, or held positions we absolutely needed! Y-yes! Like the [Fighter], for instance······!”
“Let’s stop wasting words. You seem to think that if you stall with this conversation, the other nobles will come to rescue you······ They won’t.”
“H-haha. What do you mean?”
“The citizens only fear the [Executioners]. Without them, even nobles can’t easily invade the citizens’ district.”
Perhaps thinking all was lost, Han Myungoh began struggling harder. He glared at me with reddened eyes and yelled at the top of his lungs.
“If you kill me, you’ll incur the ‘Demon King’s’ wrath!”
Once, those words would have frightened me.
“Do I look like someone who fears a ‘Demon King’?”

I raised my constellation Status. Only faintly, so the dukes of the [Industrial Complexes] and Demon Kings of other realms would not notice. But however faint it was, it was still the Status of a constellation, and enough to cow Han Myungoh.
Resignation finally settled into Han Myungoh’s trembling eyes.
“······What do you want from me?”
That was the question I had been waiting for.
Han Myungoh had connections to the demons here, after all. If he had any use, it was wise to make the most of it.
“An Oath of Existence. You know what that is, right?”
“Take it if you want to live. Otherwise, go outside and let the citizens beat you to fucking death.”
Han Myungoh sighed.
“What do you want me to swear?”
“You will not obstruct the revolution. You will not lie. You will answer my questions properly and cooperate with me with all your heart and strength.”
“······For how long?”
“Let’s make it one year.”
“Damn it······.”
It was best to set a ‘time limit’ for an oath this coercive.
Forcing someone to take a permanent oath could drive them mad.
The other person would agree to the oath more readily if you gave them hope that it could end someday.
“······All right. I swear.”
A faint spark leaped from Han Myungoh’s heart, completing the oath.
Only then did I begin asking Han Myungoh the questions I had wanted to ask.
“Department Manager Han Myungoh. How have you stayed alive all this time?”
Han Myungoh began his story.
The hardships he had endured after parting with us at Chungmuro, how he had been knocked around, and how difficult it had all been for him······.
It was so obvious he was trying to make himself sound as pitiful as possible that I interrupted him.
“Enough of that. Just tell me the important parts.”
“W-which parts?”
“You were definitely cursed by a Demon King back then. So how on earth did you become his subordinate? Asmodeus couldn’t have been that easy to win over.”
Asmodeus, one of the 72 Demon Kings.
However glib Han Myungoh might be, there was no way he had the ability to charm that bastard.
Nor did Han Myungoh possess a particularly unique story.
Beings on the level of Demon Kings were just as jaded by stories as high-ranking constellations.
The story of someone who had merely been a department manager at a large corporation’s subsidiary could hardly satisfy them.
Han Myungoh kept moving his lips for a long while before his face began to twist in misery.
I was about to press him again when Han Myungoh opened his mouth.
“······I gave birth.”
“Pardon?”
Wondering whether I had misheard, I was about to ask another question when Han Myungoh burst into tears and continued.
“I gave birth to a child!”
Unfortunately, Han Myungoh could not finish what he was saying.
By disclosing part of his contract with Asmodeus, he had incurred the penalty of losing consciousness.
It had cut off just as things were getting interesting, which dampened my mood a little.
「Kim Dokja thought. So, at any rate, the Demon Kings and constellations have started taking an interest in this world.」
The land of abandoned scenarios, the ‘Demon Realm.’
This world, long ignored by the constellations, was beginning to attract their attention again.
―Humans can’t beat them! Compared to those bastards, we’re nothing but insignificant bugs!

Han Myungoh had said that several times. Perhaps because he had spent the past few months being knocked around in the Demon Realm, he knew a great deal about the demon species’ high-ranking nobles and Demon Kings.
His despair was not entirely beyond my understanding.
Even Yoo Joonghyuk had, in fact, struggled terribly in this ‘Demon Realm.’
Of course, that was Yoo Joonghyuk’s story, not mine.
Grrrgle.
Perhaps because I had been awake all night, my stomach was clamoring for food for the first time in a while.
I went out to the tavern and asked Mark to make me something simple. Jang Hayoung was sitting at a table with a vacant expression. I quietly approached and plopped down.
“Eek!”
“You make that noise every time.”
Jang Hayoung glared at me with an irritated expression and shouted,
“What! What! What have you come to pick a fight about this time!”
“Why do you look so glum?”
“······Mind your own business.”
“Why? What happened?”
Rather than readily answering my question, Jang Hayoung picked at the food on the table. Knowing that pressing for an answer was not always the best approach, I waited.
Whatever Mark made of the sight of me and Jang Hayoung, he kept throwing smarmy winks our way. After a while, Jang Hayoung spoke.
“Why did you let me join the ‘revolutionary army’?”
“What?”
“I’m neither the [Guardian] nor the [Revolutionary]. I’m not even the chair of the citizens’ council, like Aileen.”
[The character ‘Jang Hayoung’ activates ‘Lethargy Lv.4.’]
[The character ‘Jang Hayoung’ activates ‘Self-Loathing Lv.10.’]
Damn it, here we go.
I had forgotten for a moment.
That while Yoo Joonghyuk suffered from ‘Regression Depression,’ this one was riddled with thoroughgoing ‘Self-Loathing.’
Thinking about it that way, it seemed none of the protagonists of ‘Ways of Survival’ were in their right minds.
Small, trembling shoulders. Patting those shoulders might make me feel better, but it would probably do little to comfort Hayoung.
[Your understanding of the character ‘Jang Hayoung’ has increased!]
Jang Hayoung was watching the people passing outside the window. I caught a glimpse of Aileen dealing with the aftermath of yesterday’s incident. Jang Hayoung spoke again.
“······Night will come again. Will you be able to protect everyone then, too?”
“Probably not.”
I answered honestly.
“Even I don’t know every [Executioner]. Catching them all before tomorrow night is impossible.”
There were still seven Executioners I had not caught.
If those seven set their minds to hacking people apart, tomorrow night really would become a festival of blood. I added, before Jang Hayoung could sink into despair,
“But that doesn’t mean there’s no way to stop them. We just have to find the [Fighter].”
Fighter. The only position that could fight the [Executioners] at Night.
If we could just find someone with that position, turning the tide back in our favor would not be impossible.
But Mark, who was bringing out the food, interrupted.
“······Unfortunately, there probably is no [Fighter].”
“What? How do you know that, Mark?”
“Because no one inherited the previous [Fighter’s] skill.”
Unlike the game’s other positions, [Fighter] could only be inherited by being ‘passed down.’ Mark continued.
“After the [Fighter] who protected the previous [Revolutionary] died, there was no successor.”
I already knew that.

There really was no [Fighter] in this [Industrial Complex], and that had caused Yoo Joonghyuk a great deal of trouble in the original novel, too. I took a bite of the sandwich Mark had brought and said,
“If there isn’t one, we can make one. We just need to inherit the position from another Fighter.”
“But as far as I know, there are no [Fighters] left in the 73rd Demon Realm.”
“We won’t look in the Demon Realm.”
“What?”
I glanced at Jang Hayoung.
It was about time.
I poked Jang Hayoung, whose expression had gone vacant again, and said,
“Hey, try talking to the ‘wall.’”
“W-what are you talking about?”
“That ‘wall’ you have. The ‘wall’ that stops you whenever you try to learn something.”
“H-how do you know about that ‘wall’?”
Startled, Jang Hayoung demanded an answer.
“I have my ways.”
I answered with a sly smile.
Others had no way of knowing it, but Jang Hayoung had a ‘wall.’
More precisely, a ‘wall’ called the [Unidentifiable Wall].
And until now, that wall had obstructed Jang Hayoung’s growth.
“Because of that wall, you haven’t been able to learn any skills or, well, anything like that, right? That’s why you’ve ended up like this. The lethargy, the self-loathing······.”
“W-what?”
“I know you think it’s the ‘wall at the limits of your talent.’ But it isn’t a ‘wall at the limits of your talent.’ It has an entirely different purpose.”
“No, I’m asking how you know all that······!”
“Anyway, hurry up and talk to it. You can talk to that ‘wall,’ can’t you?”

At the mention of being able to talk to the wall, Jang Hayoung’s face flushed red. I wanted to say there was nothing to worry about. I was in the same boat, talking to a wall myself. After some hesitation, Jang Hayoung slowly spoke.
“Hurry.”
A moment later, Jang Hayoung activated the skill.
[The character ‘Jang Hayoung’ activates ‘Unidentifiable Wall Lv.1’!]
Jang Hayoung’s pupils turned white.
Though I could not see them, Jang Hayoung’s field of vision was probably now surrounded by pure white walls.
Pure white walls with nothing written on them.
If walls like that blocked you every time you tried to learn a skill, developing a mental illness would hardly be strange.
Jang Hayoung spoke cautiously.
“Um······ Wall-nim?”
The moment Jang Hayoung said that, surprisingly, I heard the message, too.
[‘Unidentifiable Wall’ scowls.]
I was not sure why.
Perhaps it was because I also had something like a ‘wall.’
Whatever the reason, I thought it was fortunate.
[‘Unidentifiable Wall’ looks at its master.]
[‘Unidentifiable Wall’ says, ‘You are not yet qualified.’]
Just as prickly as in the original novel, I see.
I had been prepared for that.
“Hey, don’t be like that. Just give permission. This kid will die if you don’t help.”
Startled by my sudden words, Jang Hayoung looked at me.
The next moment, the ‘Unidentifiable Wall’ spoke.
[‘Unidentifiable Wall’ says, ‘What are you?’]
[‘Unidentifiable Wall’ says, ‘How can you hear my voice?’]
“Who I am isn’t important. Anyway, just give permission. At level 1, at least the basic functions can be used, right? Why are you blocking them?”
[‘Unidentifiable Wall’ frowns.]
Tzzzzzzzt!
As though my words had angered it, sparks were flying around Jang Hayoung. Enough probability to pressure even me, a constellation. A Myth-grade attribute really did seem to be in a class of its own.
······This isn’t going as smoothly as I expected.
I took a step back from Jang Hayoung.
The sparks suddenly bursting in midair had startled both Mark and the tavern’s customers. I evacuated them as a precaution, then spoke again.
“Are you going to keep being this prickly? It won’t do you any good. If this kid dies, won’t finding a new host be difficult for you, too?”
Tzzzzzzzt!
Another surge of probability sparks. The sheer fact that a single skill, rather than a constellation, could generate such force was practically a measure of Jang Hayoung’s potential.
That was why I absolutely had to awaken Jang Hayoung here.
[‘Unidentifiable Wall’ says, ‘What an insolent bastard.’]

The sparks bursting around Jang Hayoung’s body began to grow more intense. I had not expected such a violent reaction, so I was a little flustered myself. Just as I thought a small probability storm might erupt here,
[The exclusive skill ‘Fourth Wall’ activates strongly!]
With a tzzzzt, the sparks raging around us abruptly fell quiet. More precisely, it seemed that larger sparks had swallowed the surrounding ones.
[‘Fourth Wall’ greets ‘Unidentifiable Wall.’]
[‘Unidentifiable Wall’ is startled.]
I was startled, too.
Could the ‘walls’ actually talk to each other?
[‘Fourth Wall’ warmly greets ‘Unidentifiable Wall.’]
I saw Jang Hayoung’s face alternate between red and pale.
Hayoung must have been watching this, too.
[Fourth Wall] spoke once more.
「Fri end.」
[‘Unidentifiable Wall’ begins to tremble.]
I had no idea what was passing between the two walls, but that greeting alone was causing the air around Jang Hayoung to distort in an inexplicable manner.
[‘Unidentifiable Wall’ says, ‘Y-you, what······!’]
Then the air around me faintly stirred.
[Fourth Wall] was moving differently than usual.
I could not quite describe it. But it definitely.
Tzzzzzzzt!
Seemed to be angry.
[‘Unidentifiable Wall’ cries out in pain!]
[‘Unidentifiable Wall’ cries out in pain!]
[‘Unidentifiable Wall’ cries out in pain!]
Amid dazzling sparks, Jang Hayoung clutched at their own head and screamed.
How much time passed after that?
Somehow seeming thoroughly intimidated, the ‘Unidentifiable Wall’ displayed a message.
[‘Unidentifiable Wall’ says, ‘W-who might you be?’]
Honestly, I did not really know why Jang Hayoung had a ‘wall’ like this, either.

Even ‘Ways of Survival’ did not explain exactly what the ‘Unidentifiable Wall’ was. I had expected it to tell me by the ending······ Of course, that did not mean I had no idea whatsoever of what this wall might be.
My guess was that the existence of this ‘wall’ probably had something to do with Jang Hayoung’s occupation before traveling between dimensions.
“Th-this has never happened before······.”
Jang Hayoung was staring into the air with a deeply bewildered expression.
[‘Unidentifiable Wall’ has acknowledged the incarnation ‘Jang Hayoung’ as its master.]
The process had been rather troublesome, but with the help of [Fourth Wall], Jang Hayoung had succeeded in earning the ‘Unidentifiable Wall’s’ acknowledgment.
And for the first time in Jang Hayoung’s life, a new window appeared.
[Enter the modifier or true name of the being you wish to message.]
Perhaps thanks to [Fourth Wall], I could see that message, too.
Jang Hayoung turned to me and asked,
“······Wh-what is this? It’s telling me to enter something?”
In fact, this ability was the very reason I was determined to take ‘Jang Hayoung’ with me.
Only by borrowing the power of ‘Jang Hayoung’s’ ‘wall’ could I build up the strength to stand against those damned nebulas.
“Try entering the names I give you.”
I named several people.
All were people who had once fought as [Fighters] in the Demon Realm in the original ‘Ways of Survival.’ The next moment, another window appeared.
[Enter the message you wish to send.]
“What should I write?”
“I want to become a ‘Fighter.’ Please help me.”
“······Will that work?”
“Who knows. Just try it.”
Jang Hayoung sent the message.
And we waited with eager anticipation.
One minute, two minutes. Three minutes······ ten minutes.
Jang Hayoung asked,
“Are you sure it actually went through?”
“······Looks like it didn’t work.”
Honestly, this damned <Star Stream> had no consideration for newbies.
We were so desperately asking for help, yet not a single person had sent a reply.
After that, we wrote and sent several more messages.
[I’m looking for someone who can make me a ‘Fighter.’]
[I need your ‘Fighter’ skill.]
[Please help me.]
But no matter how many messages we sent, no reply came.
They probably thought it was spam and were ignoring it······ Damn it.
Since I had no talent for writing, I had absolutely no idea what kind of message would get a reply.
A shame Han Sooyoung wasn’t here at a time like this.
She would have come up with a good idea.
After thinking for a moment with furrowed brows, Jang Hayoung spoke.
“······We just need to get a reply first, right? Can I try writing whatever I want?”
“Have you thought of something?”
Jang Hayoung gave a small nod and typed a message.
[I’m a fifteen-year-old middle school girl.]
“Hey, wait―”
But before I could stop it, Jang Hayoung pressed the send button.
[No recipient was entered. The message has been sent to random constellations.]
It was not even addressed to anyone in particular.
I shouted in exasperation.
“These are constellations we’re dealing with! How could something like that possibly work?”
“······Just wait.”
What on earth was wrong with this kid······.
But the next moment.
[A reply has arrived!]
We looked at each other blankly, then checked the reply.
Surprisingly, the constellation who had replied was one I knew.
[Sender ― Abyssal Black Flame Dragon].
Once Jang Hayoung started talking in earnest with the ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon,’ Hayoung began grinning away. What was so entertaining? I watched, then offered a mild rebuke.
“What’s so funny?”
“It’s just the way he talks.”
Jang Hayoung was strange enough for talking about that exalted great constellation as though he were a friend, but the Abyssal Black Flame Dragon who had sent the reply was even more ridiculous.
Why was this bastard replying to random messages instead of paying attention to Han Sooyoung?
Then Jang Hayoung shook their head, as though defending the Black Flame Dragon.
“I don’t think he’s as bad as you think.”
“What nonsense is that? Has he already won you over?”
“He’s more of a gentleman when he talks than I expected, too.”
“A gentleman? What kind of gentleman replies to ‘I’m a fifteen-year-old middle school girl’?”
I was about to snap that surely I did not need to spell out the sordid implications when Jang Hayoung answered.
“He says he only replied because I’m fifteen.”
“What? He replied because you’re fifteen? What a complete piece of shit.”
I had known the Abyssal Black Flame Dragon was cruel and out of his mind, but learning his tastes ran that way suddenly made me a little worried about Han Sooyoung.
“Why are you getting so worked up? He says he’s just happy to have a friend. He’s fifteen, too.”
“What bullshit! I don’t know how old he really is, but how could there possibly be a fifteen-year-old constellation?”
And at that moment, a detail of the setting suddenly came back to me.

「Constellations living within the age-old flow of the <Star Stream> are accustomed to confining themselves within fixed frameworks to preserve their sense of self. A typical example is ‘age’: they tend to identify with a particular age of a particular life-form and think of themselves as being that age.」
······Could it be?
But even so, identifying with a fifteen-year-old? Seriously?
―Aaaaaaaargh!
That was when a scream came from inside the treatment room.
It was Han Myungoh’s.
Turning toward it, I spoke to the startled Jang Hayoung.
“Keep talking for a bit. I’ll be right back.”
“Okay. What should I ask?”
“Just leave him alone. He isn’t a [Fighter] anyway. Talk to someone else instead. You have that list I gave you earlier, right? Try contacting them again.”
Jang Hayoung nodded.
That somehow delighted expression made me uneasy, but I figured it would be fine. It was Hayoung’s own ability, after all.

The ‘Unidentifiable Wall’ had awakened a little earlier than in the original novel, but for now, this was the best option. Without the wall’s help, revolution in the [Industrial Complex] would be impossible.
When I opened the treatment room door, the now-awake Han Myungoh was looking at me in a cold sweat.
“Why did I pass out?”
I quietly closed the treatment room door and answered.
“You fainted while remembering the pain of childbirth.”
Perhaps he had had a nightmare while unconscious; sweat was pouring down Han Myungoh’s forehead.
“Was that all?”
“I think you cursed Asmodeus a little, too.”
“That son of a bitch······.”
He was also expressing his hatred for the Demon King more openly than before.
Normally, that would have been dangerous. But with the power of the [Four Tiger Evil Cutting Sword] keeping us out of Asmodeus’s sight, a little swearing would not kill him.
I pulled up a chair again and sat down.
“Let’s hear it again. What was that about giving birth, and why did Asmodeus favor you?”
“······First, I need to explain why I became pregnant.”
“I can more or less guess. Wasn’t it because of the ‘Dark Keeper’ we fought before?”

Just before we parted, Han Myungoh had been parasitized by the tentacles of the [Dark Keeper] in the [Dark Fold]. Normally, that did not immediately make someone conceive a demon, but it seemed to have worked instantly on Han Myungoh.
“That was the trigger. But it wasn’t what made me pregnant.”
“It was the curse.”

Back then, Han Myungoh had contributed to the final blow against the ‘Dark Keeper’ and received ‘Asmodeus’s’ curse. Asmodeus’s curse consumed probability to bring about whatever its target considered ‘the most terrible thing.’ In other words······.
“I see. But is that possible? Giving birth in a male body······.”
“Please don’t ask me about that part.”
I gave a small nod.
It was the least respect I could show an older man who had undergone an unbelievable experience.
We were silent for a while.
All at once, talking with Han Myungoh like this felt unfamiliar.
「Kim Dokja thought. What a strange feeling.」

Before the apocalypse, when I had been ‘Kim Dokja, office worker,’ Han Myungoh had simply been someone I found difficult to deal with. One of the bosses I most wanted to avoid. Those days had certainly existed. Days when a 3,000-won convenience-store lunch could lift or crush my spirits, and I had to count out my remaining youth in the pay slips that arrived each month.
But those days were all gone.
And now Kim Dokja and Han Myungoh, no longer employee and department manager, were sitting together and talking about a ‘Demon King.’
“Kim Dok······ no, Yoo Joonghyuk-ssi. Do you know what it means to become a father?”
Han Myungoh’s sudden question caught me a little off guard.
“Of course I don’t.”
“Now I do.”
Truthfully, I found it difficult to decide whether Han Myungoh should be called a father or a mother, but it was not important, so I let it go. Department Manager Han Myungoh’s face was serious.
“It was painful.”
Those words sounded far more painful than the hundred bits of nonsense Han Myungoh had spouted until now.
“And I was happy.”

Through the War of Kings.
Through the five disasters.

Han Myungoh slowly raised his head and looked at me.

Planet Lugratia.

Having survived that way.

‘The 73rd Demon Realm······.’

Even though I wasn’t the one who needed comforting.
“Thank you.”

Someone among the constellations who might help us.

A Kim Dokja different from the one Han Sooyoung knew.

In a place with no one else.
Kim Dokja, looking up at the sky alone in a world where he knew no one.

Having someone who worries about you this much.
